newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Escondida drills new sulphides deposit.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Escondida drills new sulphides deposit.

text.p: Drilling at Chile's Escondida copper mine has revealed a large sulphide deposit which is similar in size to the pit's Escondida North ore body, said the pit's technical manager David Borries.
"From the drilling we could say there is a significant sulphide ore body similar to Escondida North," Borries told a mining seminar in Santiago.
The results at the deposit, known as Carmen, are preliminary as they are based on a small amount of drilling, he said.
Escondida North, an extension of the ore vein mined by Outokumpu's Zaldivar, contains at least 400 million
tonnes of mineral with an average 1.3 percent copper grade.
Escondida North is in the pre-feasibility stage and is likely to come into production in around 2001.
Escondida, owned by Britain's RTZ Corp plc and Australia's Broken Hill Proprietary, also has oxide reserves of over 300 million tonnes including 70 million tonnes associated with Escondida North.
